content:
Apple is preparing to launch several new Home products, but according to the latest report from Bloomberg, the company is also working on a home security and surveillance service, expected to debut in 2027.

Apple's home security and surveillance service is expected to launch in 2027, with information coming from Mark Gurman

Apple is about to embark on a major revamp of its Home product lineup, including a new Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini, a home control hub (HomePad), and several other new products expected to appear in the near future.

Mark Gurman detailed Apple's product roadmap in his latest report, noting that the company's home ambitions also include a service.

When discussing products expected to launch in 2027, Gurman wrote:

The final sentence is crucial: "The new service will be used in a brand-new home security and surveillance service."

Gurman had previously hinted that Apple intended to enter the home security space, but now it appears the company is indeed planning to launch an actual service.

Home security and surveillance is a massive market with significant potential to boost the profitability of Apple's services business.

If Apple does launch a paid home security and surveillance service, it could also bundle it into the Apple One package to enhance appeal and retain more subscribers.

The emergence of this new service also seems to be a positive sign, indicating that Apple is indeed committed to seriously developing the smart home space. In other words, new products like this security sensor may just be the first step in expanding the product lineup.
